# Column breaks at the writing-area boundary

These eleven original controls are generated by
`tools/column_break_boundary_fixture.py` using the repository's original
exhausted-cell-indents package scaffold. No corpus text or embedded fonts are
included. Committed DOCX bytes were opened read-only by the reference application and
exported to the corresponding PDFs. JSON references record both hashes and
pypdf text positions. ZIP timestamps may change on regeneration.

Arial 10 pt text uses exact 12 pt lines on half-letter pages with half-inch
margins. Twenty-seven lines fill the writing height exactly. In `full`, the
following paragraph starts with a column break: The reference application places `After` in column
two of the same page. Before the fix, automatic line overflow followed by the
authored break put it in column one of page two. `near` leaves one line free.

The other controls cover a single-column section, repeated breaks, a terminal
break followed by another paragraph, a 36 pt break run with minimum line height,
and a preceding paragraph with keep-with-next. The terminal control retains
the paragraph-mark line in the destination column before the next paragraph.

Four spacing controls use 12 pt paragraph-before spacing: ordinary, suppressed
with `suppressSpBfAfterPgBrk`, preceded by 6 pt after-spacing, and repeated
breaks. The reference application carries a 12, 0, 6, and 12 pt gap respectively to the text after
the break(s). The rule parallels the existing page-break compatibility behavior.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.3.1 and 17.18.4 define advancing to the next column/page;
§17.3.1.33 defines paragraph spacing. Part 4 §14.8.3.42 describes deferred
spacing and its suppression for page breaks. The reference application's application of that rule
to column breaks is an observed compatibility extension; these controls do not
establish a contradiction of a normative column-break spacing requirement.

Tests cover native geometry, hit testing, editing, undo, OPC preservation and
export/reopen, alongside the existing page-break and continuous-section tests.
Native baseline comparisons require Arial; this is not a pixel-raster match.
